easy.def: A paper that lets you go in or ride.
examples: I bought a movie ticket.
Show your ticket.
The train ticket was cheap.

more.def: A piece of paper or card that shows you have paid to enter or travel.
examples: We bought tickets to the circus.
She showed her ticket to the bus driver.
The movie ticket cost eight dollars.
My room is tidy now.
Keep your desk tidy.
She has tidy hair.

more.def: Neat, with everything in its proper place.
examples: He keeps his desk tidy so he can find things easily.
The garden had tidy rows of beans.
His handwriting is small and tidy.
Tie your shoes.
She tied a bow.
Dad tied the rope.

more.def: To fasten something by making a knot in string, rope or cloth.
examples: Tie a ribbon around the gift.
He tied the boat to the dock.
She tied her shoes before running.

easy.def: A strip of cloth worn around the neck.
examples: Dad wears a tie.
His tie is blue.
The tie has stripes.

more.def: A long strip of cloth worn around the neck under a shirt collar.
examples: He wore a striped tie to picture day.
Dad knotted his tie before work.
The waiter wore a black tie.

easy.def: A game that ends with the same score on both sides.
examples: The game ended in a tie.
It was a tie.
The score is a tie.

more.def: A result in a game or contest where both sides have the same score.
examples: The soccer game ended in a tie, two to two.
The race ended in a tie.
There was a tie for first place.
These shoes are tight.
She gave me a tight hug.
The lid is tight.

more.def: Fitting closely, with no extra room or looseness.
examples: These shoes are too tight for my feet.
She gave her grandma a tight hug.
The lid on the jar was tight.
Hold on tight!
She held the rope tight.
Close the lid tight.
Hold on tight to the railing.
The box was tied tight.
She shut her eyes tight.
Wait till noon.
I played till dinner.
School is open till three.

more.def: Up to a certain time; until.
examples: The store is open till nine at night.
We stayed up till midnight on New Year's Eve.
The pool is open from morning till sunset.
Stay here till Mom comes.
Keep stirring till it is smooth.
I will wait till you finish.

more.def: Up to the time when something happens.
examples: Stir the batter till it is smooth.
We kept playing till it got dark.
Please wait till the light turns green.

easy.def: What clocks tell us, like hours and minutes.
examples: What time is it?
It is time for bed.
We have no time.

more.def: The hours, days, and years that pass, or a certain point or period measured by a clock or calendar.
examples: Time passes quickly when you are having fun.
The play starts at a different time on Sundays.
In the time of the dinosaurs, there were no people.

easy.def: One turn of something that happens again and again.
examples: I read it three times.
This is the first time I swam.
Say it one more time.

more.def: One occasion when something happens, which may happen again.
examples: It was the first time that she had ridden a horse.
I have been to the aquarium four times.
Each time we visit, the baby has grown bigger.
An ant is tiny.
The baby has tiny toes.
A tiny bug sat on my hand.
A tiny seed can grow into a giant tree.
There was a tiny crack in the glass.
The kitten was so tiny that it fit in my hand.
The tip of the pencil is sharp.
The tip of my nose is cold.
The tip of the iceberg.

more.def: The end part of something long or pointed.
examples: The tip of the pencil broke.
The cat's tail has a white tip.
The tip of the mountain was covered in snow.
I have a tip for you.
Here is a tip.
Cooking tips.

more.def: A small piece of helpful advice.
examples: She gave me a tip for tying my shoes.
The coach shared a tip about passing.
Here is a tip: read the directions first.
We left a tip.
Dad gave the waiter a tip.
The driver got a tip.

more.def: A small amount of money given to someone who has helped you.
examples: We left a tip for the waiter.
Dad gave the driver a tip.
The delivery person got a big tip.
I am tired after the race.
The baby is tired.
She felt tired at bedtime.

more.def: Feeling that you need to rest or sleep.
examples: He was tired after climbing the steep hill.
The tired puppy fell asleep on the rug.
I felt tired after staying up late.
I am tired of rain.
She is tired of waiting.
He got tired of the game.

more.def: Having had enough of something because it has gone on too long.
examples: I am tired of eating the same lunch every day.
They got tired of waiting in the long line.
She grew tired of the noisy game.
